```python:scripts/download_ds.py
import os
import shutil
import urllib.request
import gzip
import tarfile
import zipfile
import pandas as pd

directed_graphs_links = [
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/p2p-Gnutella31.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/cit-HepTh.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/soc-Epinions1.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/wiki-Vote.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/cit-HepPh.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/wiki-topcats.txt.gz",
"http://konect.cc/files/download.tsv.wikipedia_link_en.tar.bz2", # http://konect.cc/networks/wikipedia_link_en/
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/email-EuAll.txt.gz", # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/email-EuAll.html
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/wiki-Talk.txt.gz", # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/wiki-Talk.html
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/soc-LiveJournal1.txt.gz", # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/soc-LiveJournal1.html
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/soc-pokec-relationships.txt.gz" # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/soc-Pokec.html
]

undirected_graphs_links = [
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/bigdata/communities/com-amazon.ungraph.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/email-Enron.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/ca-GrQc.txt.gz",
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/bigdata/communities/com-youtube.ungraph.txt.gz",
"http://konect.cc/files/download.tsv.actor-collaboration.tar.bz2", # http://konect.cc/networks/actor-collaboration/
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/bigdata/communities/com-dblp.ungraph.txt.gz", # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/com-DBLP.html
"http://snap.stanford.edu/data/ca-AstroPh.txt.gz" # http://snap.stanford.edu/data/ca-AstroPh.html
]

all_links = directed_graphs_links + undirected_graphs_links

# Determine paths relative to the script location
script_dir = os.path.dirname(os.path.abspath(__file__))
# Assuming script is in scripts/, put datasets in the parent directory
project_root = os.path.dirname(script_dir)
datasets_dir = os.path.join(project_root, "datasets")
graph_experiments_paths = os.path.join(script_dir, "graphs_experiments.csv")

if not os.path.exists(datasets_dir):
    os.makedirs(datasets_dir)

filepaths = []

with open(graph_experiments_paths, "w") as graphs_list_file:
    graphs_list_file.write("graph_name;directed\n")
    for link in all_links:
        filepath = link.rfind("/")
        filepath = link[filepath+1:]
        print(filepath)
        filepaths.append(filepath)
        
        name = filepath
        name = name.replace(".gz","")
        name = name.replace(".zip","")
        name = name.replace(".tar","")
        name = name.replace(".bz2","")
        name = name.replace("download.tsv.","")
        
        if ".txt" not in name:
            name = name + ".txt"
            
        if link in undirected_graphs_links:
            graphs_list_file.write(name+";U\n")
        else:
            graphs_list_file.write(name+";D\n")

print(f"\nDownloading datasets to {datasets_dir}...")

# Create a custom opener to avoid 403 Forbidden errors on some sites
opener = urllib.request.build_opener()
opener.addheaders = [('User-agent', 'Mozilla/5.0')]
urllib.request.install_opener(opener)

for link in all_links:
    filename = link.split("/")[-1]
    dest_path = os.path.join(datasets_dir, filename)
    
    if not os.path.exists(dest_path):
        print(f"Downloading {filename}...")
        try:
            urllib.request.urlretrieve(link, dest_path)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Failed to download {link}: {e}")
    else:
        print(f"{filename} already exists. Skipping.")

print("\nExtracting datasets...")
for filepath in filepaths:
    full_path = os.path.join(datasets_dir, filepath)
    
    if not os.path.exists(full_path):
        continue

    if ".zip" in filepath:
        print(f"Unzipping {filepath}...")
        try:
            with zipfile.ZipFile(full_path, 'r') as zip_ref:
                zip_ref.extractall(datasets_dir)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error unzipping {filepath}: {e}")

    if ".gz" in filepath and ".tar" not in filepath:
        print(f"Decompressing {filepath}...")
        out_path = os.path.join(datasets_dir, filepath.replace(".gz", ""))
        try:
            with gzip.open(full_path, 'rb') as f_in:
                with open(out_path, 'wb') as f_out:
                    shutil.copyfileobj(f_in, f_out)
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error decompressing {filepath}: {e}")

    if ".tar.bz2" in filepath:
        print(f"Extracting {filepath}...")
        try:
            with tarfile.open(full_path, "r:bz2") as tar:
                tar.extractall(datasets_dir)
        except Exception as e:
             print(f"Error extracting {filepath}: {e}")

    if "download.tsv." in filepath:
        filepath_ = filepath.replace("download.tsv.","")
        filepath_ = filepath_.replace(".tar.bz2","")
        
        src_file = os.path.join(datasets_dir, filepath_, "out." + filepath_)
        dest_file = os.path.join(datasets_dir, filepath_ + ".txt")
        
        if os.path.exists(src_file):
            print(f"Copying {src_file} to {dest_file}")
            shutil.copy(src_file, dest_file)
        
print("\nVerifying graph files...")
try:
    graphs = pd.read_csv(graph_experiments_paths, sep=";")
    graphs_list = graphs["graph_name"].values
    for graph_filename in graphs_list:
        if not os.path.isfile(os.path.join(datasets_dir, graph_filename)):
            print("Graph file for ", graph_filename, " not found!")
    print("Verification complete.")
except Exception as e:
    print(f"Error verifying graphs: {e}")
```

I will create a MATLAB script `scripts/convert_to_mat.m` that reads the `graphs_experiments.csv` file, processes each graph dataset (handling both SNAP's `#` and Konect's `%` comment styles), converts them to a sparse logical adjacency matrix (1-based indexing), and saves them as `.mat` files with the variable name `x`.

```matlab:scripts/convert_to_mat.m
function convert_to_mat()
    %CONVERT_TO_MAT Converts graph text files to Matlab .mat files with sparse adjacency matrix 'x'.
    
    scriptPath = fileparts(mfilename('fullpath'));
    datasetPath = fullfile(scriptPath, '..', 'datasets');
    csvPath = fullfile(scriptPath, 'graphs_experiments.csv');
    
    if ~isfile(csvPath)
        error('graphs_experiments.csv not found at %s', csvPath);
    end
    
    opts = detectImportOptions(csvPath);
    opts.Delimiter = ';';
    opts.VariableNamingRule = 'preserve';
    T = readtable(csvPath, opts);
    
    for i = 1:height(T)
        fName = T.graph_name{i};
        if iscell(fName)
            fName = fName{1};
        end
        
        dirVal = T.directed{i};
        if iscell(dirVal)
            dirVal = dirVal{1};
        end
        isDirected = strcmpi(strtrim(dirVal), 'D');
        
        inputFile = fullfile(datasetPath, fName);
        [~, name, ~] = fileparts(fName);
        outputFile = fullfile(datasetPath, [name, '.mat']);
        
        fprintf('Processing %s...\n', fName);
        
        if ~isfile(inputFile)
            warning('File not found: %s', inputFile);
            continue;
        end
        
        fid = fopen(inputFile, 'r');
        if fid == -1
            warning('Could not open file: %s', inputFile);
            continue;
        end
        
        data = textscan(fid, '%f %f %*[^\n]', 'CommentStyle', {'#', '%'});
        fclose(fid);
        
        u = data{1};
        v = data{2};
        
        if isempty(u)
            warning('No data found in %s', fName);
            continue;
        end
        
        min_id = min(min(u), min(v));
        if min_id == 0
            u = u + 1;
            v = v + 1;
        end
        
        n = max(max(u), max(v));
        
        x = sparse(u, v, true, n, n);
        
        if ~isDirected
            x = x | x';
        end
        
        x = logical(x);
        
        save(outputFile, 'x', '-v7.3');
    end
end
```

        "originalContents": "function convert_to_mat()\r\n    %CONVERT_TO_MAT Converts graph text files to Matlab .mat files with sparse adjacency matrix 'x'.\r\n    \r\n    scriptPath = fileparts(mfilename('fullpath'));\r\n    datasetPath = fullfile(scriptPath, '..', 'datasets');\r\n    csvPath = fullfile(scriptPath, 'graphs_experiments.csv');\r\n    \r\n    if ~isfile(csvPath)\r\n        error('graphs_experiments.csv not found at %s', csvPath);\r\n    end\r\n    \r\n    opts = detectImportOptions(csvPath);\r\n    opts.Delimiter = ';';\r\n    opts.VariableNamingRule = 'preserve';\r\n    T = readtable(csvPath, opts);\r\n    \r\n    for i = 1:height(T)\r\n        fName = T.graph_name{i};\r\n        if iscell(fName)\r\n            fName = fName{1};\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n        dirVal = T.directed{i};\r\n        if iscell(dirVal)\r\n            dirVal = dirVal{1};\r\n        end\r\n        isDirected = strcmpi(strtrim(dirVal), 'D');\r\n        \r\n        inputFile = fullfile(datasetPath, fName);\r\n        [~, name, ~] = fileparts(fName);\r\n        outputFile = fullfile(datasetPath, 'mat', [name, '.mat']);\r\n        \r\n        fprintf('Processing %s...\\n', fName);\r\n        \r\n        if ~isfile(inputFile)\r\n            warning('File not found: %s', inputFile);\r\n            continue;\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n        fid = fopen(inputFile, 'r');\r\n        if fid == -1\r\n            warning('Could not open file: %s', inputFile);\r\n            continue;\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n        data = textscan(fid, '%f %f %*[^\\n]', 'CommentStyle', {'#', '%'});\r\n        fclose(fid);\r\n        \r\n        u = data{1};\r\n        v = data{2};\r\n        \r\n        if isempty(u)\r\n            warning('No data found in %s', fName);\r\n            continue;\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n        min_id = min(min(u), min(v));\r\n        if min_id == 0\r\n            u = u + 1;\r\n            v = v + 1;\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n        n = max(max(u), max(v));\r\n        \r\n        x = sparse(u, v, true, n, n);\r\n        \r\n        if ~isDirected\r\n            x = x | x';\r\n        end\r\n        \r\n",

        "originalContents": "\r\n        for node_id in nodes_set:\r\n            node_ids_map[node_id] = new_node_id\r\n            new_node_id += 1\r\n\r\n        fin = open(graph_path,\"r\")\r\n        print(\"writing \",graph_path_out,\"...\")\r\n        fout = open(graph_path_out,\"w\")\r\n        fout_bav = open(graph_path_out_bav,\"w\")\r\n        for line in fin:\r\n            if \"#\" not in line and \"%\" not in line:\r\n                line = line.replace(\" \\n\",\"\")\r\n                line = line.replace(\"\\n\",\"\")\r\n                if \" \" in line or \"\\t\" in line:\r\n                    if \" \" in line:\r\n                        nodes = line.split(\" \")\r\n                    else:\r\n                        if \"\\t\" in line:\r\n                            nodes = line.split(\"\\t\")\r\n                    try:\r\n                        nodes = [int(n) for n in nodes]\r\n                    except ValueError:\r\n                        print(\"ValueError encountered!\")\r\n                        print(nodes)\r\n                        print(line)\r\n                        os.system(\"rm \"+graph_path_out)\r\n                        exit()\r\n                    if len(nodes) \u003e= 2:\r\n                        new_edge_line = str(node_ids_map[nodes[0]])+\" \"+str(node_ids_map[nodes[1]])+\"\\n\"\r\n                        new_edge_line_bav = str(node_ids_map[nodes[0]])+\"\\t\"+str(node_ids_map[nodes[1]])+\"\\n\"\r\n                        fout.write(new_edge_line)\r\n                        fout_bav.write(new_edge_line_bav)\r\n        fout.close()\r\n        fout_bav.close()\r\n\r\n\r\n        print(\"done graph\",graph)\r\n        print(max_node_id)\r\n        print(len(nodes_set))\r\n        print(\"\")\r\n    else:\r\n        print(\"skipping graph\",graph)",

        "contents": "import os\r\nimport argparse\r\nparser = argparse.ArgumentParser()\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-db\", help=\"path to graph input file\")\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-e\",\"--epsilon\", type=float ,help=\"approximation accuracy parameter (in (0,1))\",default=0.01)\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-d\",\"--delta\", type=float ,help=\"approximation confidence parameter (in (0,1), def. 0.1)\",default=0.05)\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-k\", type=int ,help=\"parameter for top-k approximation\",default=0)\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-t\",\"--type\", type=int ,help=\"type of graph. 1 means directed, 0 undirected (def. undirected)\",default=0)\r\nparser.add_argument(\"-maxtime\", type=int ,help=\"maximum seconds before killing kadabra\",default=-1)\r\nargs = parser.parse_args()\r\n\r\ndelta = args.delta\r\nfile_output_path = \"output.txt\"\r\npath_executable = \"../kadabra/kadabra\"\r\nif args.maxtime \u003e 0:\r\n    path_executable = \"timeout \"+str(args.maxtime)+\" \"+path_executable\r\noutput_path = \"results_kadabra.csv\"\r\ndirected_flag = \"\"\r\nif args.type == 1:\r\n    directed_flag = \"-d \"\r\ntopk_flag = \"\"\r\nif args.k \u003e 0:\r\n    topk_flag = \"-k \"+str(args.k)+\" \"\r\n    output_path = \"results_kadabra_topk.csv\"\r\n    file_output_path = \"output_topk.txt\"\r\ncmd = path_executable+\" \"+directed_flag+topk_flag+str(args.epsilon)+\" \"+str(delta)+\" \"+str(args.db)+\" \u003e \"+file_output_path\r\nprint(cmd)\r\nretval = os.system(cmd)\r\nif retval \u003e 0:\r\n    print(\"KADABRA terminated with errors\")\r\n    exit()\r\n\r\n\r\nif os.path.isfile(output_path) == False:\r\n    # write the header for the results\r\n    out = \"graph_name;epsilon;delta;k;type;m;time;diameter;first_samples;first_time;eps_mcera;iter_index_mcera;top1_est;top1_ub;avg_spl_est;avg_spl_ub;samples_bound;time_bfs;time_critical;eps_final_topk\\n\"\r\n    out_file = open(output_path,\"w\")\r\n    out_file.write(out)\r\n    print(out)\r\n    out_file.close()",

      "codeBlock": {
        "contents": "# SILVAN: Estimating Betweenness Centralities with Progressive Sampling and Non-uniform Rademacher Bounds #\r\n\r\nThis repository contains the implementation of SILVAN, supporting our paper [\"SILVAN: Estimating Betweenness Centralities with Progressive Sampling and Non-uniform Rademacher Bounds\"](https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3628601).\r\n\r\nSILVAN is an algorithm to compute approximations of the Betweenness Centralities from graphs with progressive sampling. More details can be found in the paper, published in ACM Transactions on Knowledge Discovery from Data: https://dl.acm.org/doi/10.1145/3628601\r\n\r\nPart of the underlying implementation of SILVAN is based on the sampling algorithm [KADABRA](https://github.com/natema/kadabra) by Michele Borassi and Emanuele Natale. Therefore, it has the same compilation dependencies (described below) and it is distributed with the same license (Apache License 2.0).\r\n\r\n## Installation\r\n\r\nThe software requires the [OpenMP API](http://openmp.org/wp/). After cloning this repository,\r\nbuild the software by issuing the &#96;make&#96; command inside the silvan folder.\r\n\r\n### Running SILVAN ###\r\n\r\nThe network has to be provided as a file containing two space-separated\r\nintegers &#96;u v&#96; per line, for each edge &#96;(u,v)&#96; of the network. The labels of\r\nthe vertices are assumed to be consecutive.\r\n\r\nTo run SILVAN, you can use the &#96;run_silvan.py&#96; python script found in the &#96;scripts&#96; folder. It takes the following input parameters:\r\n\r\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\r\nusage: run_silvan.py [-h] [-db DB] [-e EPSILON] [-d DELTA] [-a AEMPPEELING]\r\n                     [-s ALPHA] [-k K] [-mh MH] [-eempp EEMPP] [-o O]\r\n                     [-t TYPE]\r\n",

        "contents": "optional arguments:\r\n  -h, --help            show this help message and exit\r\n  -db DB                path to graph input file\r\n  -e EPSILON, --epsilon EPSILON\r\n                        approximation accuracy parameter (in (0,1))\r\n  -d DELTA, --delta DELTA\r\n                        approximation confidence parameter (in (0,1), def. 0.1)\r\n  -a AEMPPEELING, --aemppeeling AEMPPEELING\r\n                        parameter a for empirical peeling (def. = 2)\r\n  -s ALPHA, --alpha ALPHA\r\n                        parameter alpha for sampling shortest paths (def. = 2.3)\r\n  -k K                  parameter for top-k approximation\r\n  -mh MH                enable computation of m_hat (def.=1)\r\n  -eempp EEMPP          enable empirical peeling (def.=1)\r\n  -o O                  output path (def.=results_silvan.csv or results_silvan_topk.csv)\r\n  -t TYPE, --type TYPE  type of graph. 1 means directed, 0 undirected (def. undirected)\r\n&#96;&#96;&#96;\r\n\r\nFor example, to approximate the betweenness centrality of all nodes of the undirected graph &#96;graph.txt&#96; with absolute accuracy 0.01 and with probability at least 0.95, you can use\r\n\r\n&#96;python run_silvan.py -db graph.txt -e 0.01 -d 0.05&#96;\r\n\r\nor to approximate the top-10 most central nodes of the directed graph &#96;digraph.txt&#96; with relative accuracy 0.1, you can use\r\n\r\n&#96;python run_silvan.py -db digraph.txt -e 0.1 -k 10 -t 1&#96;\r\n\r\n### Reproducing experiments\r\nTo reproduce the experiments described in the paper, follow the instructions listed below.\r\n\r\n1.         "contents": "import os\r\nimport time\r\nimport numpy as np\r\nimport math\r\nimport pandas as pd\r\n\r\ngraph_experiments_paths = \"graphs_experiments.csv\"\r\ngraphs = pd.read_csv(graph_experiments_paths,sep=\";\")\r\ngraphs = graphs.set_index('graph_name').T.to_dict('list')\r\nprint(graphs)\r\n#graphs = graphs[\"graph_name\"].values\r\n\r\nnum_runs = 10\r\ndb_path = \"../datasets/\"\r\nrun_kadabra = 1\r\n\r\nepsilons = [0.01 , 0.005 , 0.0025 , 0.001 , 0.0005]\r\nprint(\"epsilons\",epsilons)\r\n\r\n\r\nfor run_id in range(num_runs):\r\n    for epsilon in epsilons:\r\n        for graph_name in graphs:\r\n            directed = graphs[graph_name]\r\n            directed = directed[0] == 'D'\r\n            directed_flag = \"\"\r\n            if directed == True:\r\n                directed_flag = \" -t 1\"\r\n            # run the experiment\r\n            graph_name = graph_name.replace(\".txt\",\"_pre.txt\")\r\n            cmd = \"python3 run_kadabra.py -db \"+db_path+graph_name+\" -e \"+str(epsilon)+directed_flag\r\n            if run_kadabra == 1:\r\n                print(\"run \",run_id,\" \",cmd)\r\n                os.system(cmd)\r\n                time.sleep(1)\r\n            cmd = \"python3 run_silvan.py -db \"+db_path+graph_name+\" -e \"+str(epsilon)+directed_flag\r\n            print(\"run \",run_id,\" \",cmd)\r\n            os.system(cmd)\r\n            time.sleep(1)",

The C++ code checks if the first character is NOT '#', and if so, it calls sscanf. But here's the key issue:

**The C++ code does NOT check if the line is empty before accessing line[0]!**

However, when `getline` reads an empty line, the string will be empty, and accessing `line[0]` might work but checking `line[0] != '#'` on an empty line would be true (since empty string's first character check might behave differently in C++).

- If sscanf can't parse two integers, it leaves u and v unchanged
- So u and v retain their previous values!

This means in the C++ code:
1. If a line has valid data, u and v are updated
2. If a line is empty or invalid, u and v keep their LAST valid values

parts = strsplit(line, {' ', '\t'}, 'CollapseDelimiters', false);

The MATLAB splitting with multiple spaces creates empty array elements, causing parsing issues.         "contents": "\r\nuint32_t Graph::estimate_diameter() {\r\n    compute_cc();\r\n    compute_cc_adj();\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"n_components \" \u003c\u003c n_components \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n\r\n    uint32_t *q = (uint32_t*) malloc(get_nn() * sizeof(uint32_t));\r\n    int32_t *dist_f = (int32_t*) malloc(get_nn() * sizeof(int32_t));\r\n    int32_t *dist_b = (int32_t*) malloc(get_nn() * sizeof(int32_t));\r\n    uint32_t *pivots = (uint32_t*) malloc(n_components * sizeof(uint32_t));\r\n    uint32_t *ecc_f_pivots_scc = (uint32_t*) malloc(n_components * sizeof(uint32_t));\r\n    uint32_t *ecc_b_pivots_scc = (uint32_t*) malloc(n_components * sizeof(uint32_t));\r\n    uint32_t *ecc_f_pivots = (uint32_t*) malloc(n_components * sizeof(uint32_t));\r\n    uint32_t diam = 0;\r\n\r\n    for (uint32_t v = 0; v \u003c get_nn(); v++) {\r\n        dist_f[v] = -1;\r\n        dist_b[v] = -1;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    compute_pivot(pivots);\r\n\r\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i \u003c n_components; i++) {\r\n        ecc_f_pivots_scc[i] = compute_ecc_in_scc(pivots[i], q, dist_f, false);\r\n        ecc_b_pivots_scc[i] = compute_ecc_in_scc(pivots[i], q, dist_b, true);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i \u003c n_components; i++) {\r\n        ecc_f_pivots[i] = ecc_f_pivots_scc[i];\r\n        for (auto cc : cc_adj[i]) {\r\n            ecc_f_pivots[i] = max(ecc_f_pivots[i],\r\n                                  ecc_f_pivots_scc[i] + 1 + ecc_b_pivots_scc[cc]\r\n                                  + ecc_f_pivots[cc]);\r\n        }\r\n        diam = max(diam, ecc_f_pivots[i] + ecc_b_pivots_scc[i]);\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    free(q);\r\n    free(dist_f);\r\n    free(dist_b);\r\n    free(pivots);\r\n    free(ecc_f_pivots_scc);\r\n    free(ecc_b_pivots_scc);\r\n\r\n    return diam;\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Add the edges (u,v) to the adjacency list of the graph.\r\n// Attention: this way, it is possible to add multiple edges\r\nvoid Graph::add_edge( const uint32_t u, const uint32_t v ) {\r\n    adj[u][degrees[u]++] = v;\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Clean the adjacency list of the graph.\r\n// Instead of de-allocating the array adj, the function set to zero the length of each entry.",

        "contents": "\r\nProbabilistic::Probabilistic( const std::string \u0026filename, const bool directed, const double verb, const double sampling_rate_, const bool alpha_given_, const double empirical_peeling_param_ , const bool enable_m_hat_, const std::string output_file_ ): Graph( filename, directed ), verbose(verb) {\r\n    approx = (double *) calloc( get_nn(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    approx_toadd = (double *) calloc( get_nn(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    time_bfs = (double *) calloc( omp_get_max_threads(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    time_comp_finished = (double *) calloc( omp_get_max_threads(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    time_critical = (double *) calloc( omp_get_max_threads(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    time_critical_round = (double *) calloc( omp_get_max_threads(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    time_mcera = (double *) calloc( omp_get_max_threads(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    emp_wimpy_vars = (double *) calloc( get_nn(), sizeof(double) );\r\n    for (uint32_t i = 0; i \u003c get_nn(); i++) {\r\n        approx[i] = 0;\r\n        approx_toadd[i] = 0;\r\n        emp_wimpy_vars[i] = 0;\r\n    }\r\n    for(int i=0; i\u003comp_get_max_threads(); i++){\r\n      time_bfs[i] = 0.;\r\n      time_comp_finished[i] = 0.;\r\n      time_critical[i] = 0.;\r\n      time_critical_round[i] = 0.;\r\n      time_mcera[i] = 0.;\r\n    }\r\n    n_pairs = 0;\r\n    vis_edges = 0;\r\n    if (verbose \u003e 0) {\r\n        print_data();\r\n    }\r\n    output_file = output_file_;\r\n    // mcrade\r\n    mcrade = (int64_t *) calloc( get_nn()*mctrials, sizeof(int64_t) );\r\n    partition_index = (int *) calloc( get_nn(), sizeof(int) );\r\n    mcrade_randgen = new Rand_gen( 2021 );\r\n    sup_bcest = 0.0;\r\n    alpha_sp_given = alpha_given_;\r\n    alpha_sp_sampling = sampling_rate_;\r\n    empirical_peeling_a = empirical_peeling_param_;\r\n    enable_m_hat = enable_m_hat_;\r\n}",

+ function [numCC, ccLabels] = find_strongly_connected_components(adj)
+     n = size(adj, 1);
+     visited = false(n, 1);
+     finishOrder = [];
+     
+     for i = 1:n
+         if ~visited(i)
+             finishOrder = dfs_finish_time(adj, i, visited, finishOrder);
+         end
+     end
+     
+     adjT = adj';
+     visited = false(n, 1);
+     ccLabels = zeros(n, 1);
+     numCC = 0;
+     
+     for i = length(finishOrder):-1:1
+         node = finishOrder(i);
+         if ~visited(node)
+             numCC = numCC + 1;
+             dfs_label(adjT, node, visited, ccLabels, numCC);
+         end
+     end
+ end
+ 
+ function finishOrder = dfs_finish_time(adj, start, visited, finishOrder)
+     stack = start;
+     visited(start) = true;
+     
+     while ~isempty(stack)
+         node = stack(end);
+         neighbors = find(adj(node, :));
+         
+         hasUnvisited = false;
+         for j = 1:length(neighbors)
+             neighbor = neighbors(j);
+             if ~visited(neighbor)
+                 visited(neighbor) = true;
+                 stack = [stack, neighbor];
+                 hasUnvisited = true;
+                 break;
+             end
+         end
+         
+         if ~hasUnvisited
+             stack(end) = [];
+             finishOrder = [finishOrder, node];
+         end
+     end
+ end
+ 
+ function dfs_label(adj, start, visited, ccLabels, label)
+     stack = start;
+     visited(start) = true;
+     ccLabels(start) = label;
+     
+     while ~isempty(stack)
+         node = stack(end);

+                 visited(neighbor) = true;
+                 ccLabels(neighbor) = label;
+                 stack = [stack, neighbor];
+             end

2. **Extracts largest component** (lines 96-102):
   - When multiple components exist, it identifies and extracts only the largest one
   - Removes isolated nodes and disconnected subgraphs
   - Re-indexes the adjacency matrix to only include the largest component

3. **Added helper functions** (lines 120-184):
   - `find_strongly_connected_components`: Implements Kosaraju's algorithm for directed graphs
   - `dfs_finish_time`: DFS to compute finish times
   - `dfs_label`: DFS to label nodes by component

**This preprocessing ensures:**
- ✅ No disconnected components (extracts largest connected component)
- ✅ No self-loops (already removed)
- ✅ Consecutive node IDs (1 to N)
- ✅ Duplicate edges handled (sparse matrix automatically handles this)

Now when you run `convert_to_mat()`, the `.mat` files will contain only the largest connected component, which should work perfectly with your MEX function! The script will also print statistics showing the original graph size and the extracted component size.

        "contents": "\r\n// maximum error allowed; union_sample and start_factor are parameters of the algorithm\r\n// that are automatically chosen.\r\nvoid Probabilistic::run(uint32_t k, double delta, double err, uint32_t union_sample, uint32_t start_factor) {\r\n    this-\u003eabsolute = (k == 0);\r\n    this-\u003eerr = err;\r\n    this-\u003edelta = delta;\r\n    start_time = get_time_sec();\r\n    graph_diameter = estimate_diameter();\r\n    //omp_set_num_threads(64);\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"estimated diameter of the graph: \" \u003c\u003c graph_diameter \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"time for estimating diameter \" \u003c\u003c get_time_sec() - start_time \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    uint32_t tau = max(1. / err * (log(1. / delta)) , 1000.);\r\n    tau = max((double)tau , 2 * graph_diameter * (log(1. / delta)) );\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"Starting first pass. Tentative number of samples: \" \u003c\u003c tau \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    num_samples = 0;\r\n    sup_bcest = 0;\r\n    sup_emp_wimpy_var = 0;\r\n    void_samples = 0;\r\n    second_phase_started = false;\r\n    enable_emp_peel = empirical_peeling_a \u003e 1;\r\n    if(!enable_emp_peel){\r\n      empirical_peeling_a = 100*tau;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n\r\n    if (union_sample == 0) {\r\n        union_sample = min(get_nn(), (uint32_t) max( 2 * sqrt(get_ne()) / omp_get_max_threads(), k+20. ));\r\n    }\r\n    this-\u003eunion_sample=union_sample;\r\n    this-\u003ek=min(k, get_nn());\r\n\r\n    sp_lengths = (uint64_t *) malloc( (graph_diameter+1)*sizeof(uint64_t) );\r\n    for( int i=0; i \u003c= graph_diameter; i++ ){\r\n        sp_lengths[i] = 0;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    last_output = get_time_sec();\r\n    start_time = get_time_sec();\r\n    this-\u003etop_k = new Ranking_list(union_sample);\r\n    srand( SEED );\r\n    uint32_t *random_seed = (uint32_t *) malloc( omp_get_max_threads()*sizeof(uint32_t) );\r\n    for( int i=0; i \u003c omp_get_max_threads(); i++ ){\r\n        random_seed[i] = rand();\r\n    }\r\n    distinct_nodes_top_k = 0;\r\n\r\n    firstpass = true;\r\n    int samples_per_step = 10;\r\n\r\n    // first phase sampling\r\n\r\n    bool stop_first_pass = false;\r\n    #pragma omp parallel\r\n",

        "originalContents": "\r\n// maximum error allowed; union_sample and start_factor are parameters of the algorithm\r\n// that are automatically chosen.\r\nvoid Probabilistic::run(uint32_t k, double delta, double err, uint32_t union_sample, uint32_t start_factor) {\r\n    this-\u003eabsolute = (k == 0);\r\n    this-\u003eerr = err;\r\n    this-\u003edelta = delta;\r\n    start_time = get_time_sec();\r\n    graph_diameter = estimate_diameter();\r\n    //omp_set_num_threads(64);\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"estimated diameter of the graph: \" \u003c\u003c graph_diameter \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"time for estimating diameter \" \u003c\u003c get_time_sec() - start_time \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    uint32_t tau = max(1. / err * (log(1. / delta)) , 1000.);\r\n    tau = max((double)tau , 2 * graph_diameter * (log(1. / delta)) );\r\n    std::cout \u003c\u003c \"Starting first pass. Tentative number of samples: \" \u003c\u003c tau \u003c\u003c std::endl;\r\n    num_samples = 0;\r\n    sup_bcest = 0;\r\n    sup_emp_wimpy_var = 0;\r\n    void_samples = 0;\r\n    second_phase_started = false;\r\n    enable_emp_peel = empirical_peeling_a \u003e 1;\r\n    if(!enable_emp_peel){\r\n      empirical_peeling_a = 100*tau;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n\r\n    if (union_sample == 0) {\r\n        union_sample = min(get_nn(), (uint32_t) max( 2 * sqrt(get_ne()) / omp_get_max_threads(), k+20. ));\r\n    }\r\n    this-\u003eunion_sample=union_sample;\r\n    this-\u003ek=min(k, get_nn());\r\n\r\n    sp_lengths = (uint64_t *) malloc( (graph_diameter+1)*sizeof(uint64_t) );\r\n    for( int i=0; i \u003c= graph_diameter; i++ ){\r\n        sp_lengths[i] = 0;\r\n    }\r\n\r\n    last_output = get_time_sec();\r\n    start_time = get_time_sec();\r\n    this-\u003etop_k = new Ranking_list(union_sample);\r\n    srand( SEED );\r\n    uint32_t *random_seed = (uint32_t *) malloc( omp_get_max_threads()*sizeof(uint32_t) );\r\n    for( int i=0; i \u003c omp_get_max_threads(); i++ ){\r\n        random_seed[i] = rand();\r\n    }\r\n    distinct_nodes_top_k = 0;\r\n\r\n    firstpass = true;\r\n    int samples_per_step = 10;\r\n\r\n    // first phase sampling\r\n\r\n    bool stop_first_pass = false;\r\n    #pragma omp parallel\r\n",

        "originalContents": "#include \u003ccstdint\u003e\r\n#include \u003cvector\u003e\r\n#include \u003cunordered_set\u003e\r\n#include \u003cfstream\u003e\r\n#include \u003ciostream\u003e\r\n#include \u003cset\u003e\r\n#include \u003cmath.h\u003e\r\n#include \"Graph.h\"\r\n#include \u003climits.h\u003e\r\n\r\nusing namespace std;\r\n\r\n// Creates an empty graph.\r\n// INPUT: The number of nodes of the graph and the list of corresponding maximum degrees.\r\n// NOTE: This constructor is used for the pred graph used in the BFS.\r\nGraph::Graph( const uint32_t nodes_num, const uint32_t *maxdegs ) {\r\n    this-\u003enodes_num = nodes_num;\r\n    edges_num = 0;\r\n    adj = (uint32_t **) malloc( nodes_num * sizeof(uint32_t *) );\r\n    degrees = (uint32_t *) malloc( nodes_num * sizeof(uint32_t ) );\r\n    cc = (uint32_t *) malloc( nodes_num * sizeof(uint32_t ) );\r\n    inc = NULL;\r\n    in_degrees = NULL;\r\n\r\n    for( uint32_t i=0; i \u003c nodes_num ; i++ ) {\r\n        degrees[i] = 0;\r\n        adj[i] = (uint32_t *) malloc( maxdegs[i] * sizeof(uint32_t) );\r\n    }\r\n}\r\n\r\n// Loads a graph from a file.\r\n// INPUT: The path to the file where the graph is stored and a boolean\r\n// which tells whether the graph is directed.\r\n// NOTE: The input format consists of a list of edges (two space-separated\r\n// integer values per line which are the two endpoints of the edge).\r\n// Multiple edges and self-loops are ignored.\r\n// This is the main costructor.",

        "contents": "\r\n    for (u = 0; u \u003c n; u++) {\r\n        if (visited[u] != 0) {\r\n            continue;\r\n        }\r\n        // Perform a DFS from u\r\n        dfs_stack_end = 1;\r\n        scc_stack_end = 0;\r\n        dfs_stack[0] = u;\r\n        pred[u] = u;\r\n\r\n        while (dfs_stack_end \u003e 0) {\r\n             v = dfs_stack[dfs_stack_end - 1];\r\n             if (visited[v] == 0) {\r\n                 // It means that this is the first time we visit v.\r\n                 // We set the index and the lowlink to be equal: during the\r\n                 // algorithm, the lowlink may decrease.\r\n                 visited[v] = 1;\r\n                 index[v] = current_index;\r\n                 lowlink[v] = current_index;\r\n                 current_index++;\r\n                 // We add v to the stack of vertices in the current SCC\r\n                 scc_stack[scc_stack_end++] = v;\r\n                 in_scc_stack[v] = 1;\r\n\r\n                 // We iterate over all neighbors of v\r\n                 for (uint32_t i = 0; i \u003c degrees[v]; i++) {\r\n                     w = adj[v][i];\r\n                     if (visited[w] == 0) {\r\n                         // Vertex w is added to the DFS stack\r\n                         pred[w] = v;\r\n                         dfs_stack[dfs_stack_end++] = w;\r\n                     }\r\n                     else if (in_scc_stack[w]) {\r\n                         // We update the lowlink of v (later, we will \"pass\"\r\n                         // this updated value to all ancestors of v.\r\n                         lowlink[v] = min(lowlink[v], lowlink[w]);\r\n                     }\r\n                 }\r\n             }",
